items.title: Mozambique: Government and partners review lessons learned from NCRP – ADIN
items.summary: The meeting served to present an assessment of the project, discuss challenges and share lessons learned as the project closes and unfinished interventions are transferred to Moz Community, also funded by the World Bank, with a budget of US$25 million Photo: ADIN – Agência de Desenvolvimento Integrado do Norte Of the 80 infrastructure projects initially planned under the NCRP, 42 were completed during the implementation period, while the remaining interventions were transferred to Moz Community, under the leadership of the Northern Integrated Development Agency (ADIN) Photo: ADIN – Agência de Desenvolvimento Integrado do Norte On the occasion, the minister highlighted the importance of institutional coordination, compliance with procurement rules and dialogue with the business sector to improve the implementation of development projects The meeting also provided an opportunity to gather contributions from businesspeople in Cabo Delgado on the participation of local companies and the implementation and supervision of works.

items.title: Government calls for coordinated international action against terrorism
items.summary: Maputo, 19 Oct (AIM) – Mozambican government calls for coordinated international action to combat terrorism and violent extremism, arguing that dialogue, diplomacy, and cooperation among states are crucial tools for addressing current global challenges. This position was presented by the Minister of Justice, Mateus Saize, at the 52nd Session of the Council of Ministers of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), held on October 17–18 in the Iraqi capital Baghdad under the motto “Dialogue and Solidarity as Fundamental Pillars for Advancing Peace and Sustainable Development.” According to the minister, terrorism, trade disputes between major global powers, and the effects of climate change – including cyclones, floods, and droughts – are key challenges currently affecting Mozambique within the international landscape. “The fight against terrorism and violent extremism must be accompanied by investments in development, education, employment, and social inclusion, with a particular focus on the youth.

items.title: Canada: Alberta votes on holding independence referendum
items.summary: Canada's oil-rich western province of Alberta is not deemed likely to vote in favor of a real breakaway plebiscite. Nevertheless the separatist movement hopes to gain leverage over Mark Carney's government Residents of Alberta in Canada are voting in a referendum on whether the province should begin a process that could ultimately lead to independence The motion does not appear likely to succeed but the vote taking place at all signifies economic and political grievances gaining some sway in the vast oil-rich region Separatist leaders hope that a comparatively strong showing for their cause could nevertheless pressure Prime Minister Mark Carney's government in Ottawa to pay them more heed in future Polls opened at 9 a.m. local time in the provincial capital Edmonton (1500 GMT/UTC) on Monday They are scheduled to close at 8 p.m.

items.title: Can diplomacy prevent an Ethiopia-Eritrea war as Tigray gets a new administration?
items.summary: Ethiopia has installed a new administration in conflict-hit Tigray after federal forces pushed back Tigrayan fighters. But tensions with Eritrea continue to raise fears of a wider regional war Ethiopia 's Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed on Friday announced an interim government in the country's northern Tigray region and gave it six months to prepare for regional elections and restore stability Abiy's announcement followed a military offensive launched in September by the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) and six other armed groups.

items.title: Catalonia's former rebel president can return to Spain, court rules
items.summary: Puigdemont pictured during his only known return to Spain since fleeing, in 2024 - an appearance which prompted a police manhunt Spain's Supreme Court has ruled the former president of Catalonia, Carles Puigdemont, can return without fear of arrest nearly a decade after going into self-imposed exile having led a failed independence bid The court upheld a decision to lift an arrest warrant for him linked to the referendum his regional government organised in 2017, in defiance of Madrid Direct rule was imposed on the region soon after the vote and Puigdemont fled to Belgium, where he has been based ever since - with a surprise appearance in Barcelona in 2024 prompting a police manhunt But the Spain to which he may return is much different from a decade ago, with Catalan independence now a marginal political issue Monday's ruling brings to an end a lengthy legal wrangle between the Spanish judiciary and the former Catalan president In 2024, Spain's socialist government introduced a controversial amnesty for dozens of Catalan politicians and activists who were involved in the secession…

items.title: Terrorists increasingly targeting civilians in three Cabo Delgado districts – ACLED
items.summary: Maputo, 19 Oct (AIM) – Islamic State Mozambique (ISM) has increasingly targeted civilians in the districts of Mocimboa da Praia, Muidumbe, and Macomia, in the southern Mozambican province of Cabo Delgado over the months of August and September. According to the latest report carried out by the independent conflict registration project ACLED (Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project), the terrorists have been tightening security measures in Mocimboa da Praia, constraining commercial and humanitarian activity. “As a result, the town is likely to become tense. That tension may be directed toward the state, either through protests or increased collaboration with ISM. Evidence suggests that ISM’s return to Nangade is to draw on support from neighboring Tanzania, a development likely to lead to tightened security measures on both sides of the border”, reads the report. Meanwhile, the early October release of hostages taken by ISM in Niassa province last month in return for ransom is likely to embolden the group to target foreigners for abduction in the future.
